verdict: Broadcom's revenue grew 28% to a record $18.0B as AI chip sales jumped 74%, and a $1.6B tax benefit — the tax line adding money instead of taking it — lifted net income to $8.5B.

kpis.label: AI semiconductor revenue
kpis.note: vs a year ago — guided to roughly double next quarter, to $8.2B

segments.name: Semiconductor solutions
segments.note: Chips — above all custom AI accelerators and networking gear for data centers. AI semiconductor revenue grew 74% YoY, and Broadcom guided it to roughly double in the next quarter.

segments.name: Infrastructure software
segments.note: VMware and other enterprise software — the steady, subscription side of the company, up 19% YoY.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Designing the next chips and software — a smaller share of each revenue dollar than most chip rivals spend.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Selling the products and running the company.

opex.name: Amortization & restructuring
opex.note: Writing down the value of brands and technology bought in acquisitions (VMware above all) — a bookkeeping charge, not cash — plus restructuring costs.

takeaways.title: AI chips are the story
takeaways.text: AI semiconductor revenue grew 74% YoY, and Broadcom guided it to roughly double in the next quarter to $8.2B — on custom AI accelerators and Ethernet AI switches.

takeaways.title: A tax benefit, not a tax bill
takeaways.text: The tax line added $1,649M instead of subtracting — including a one-time, non-cash benefit of about $2.1B as tax statutes of limitations lapsed. That is why net income of $8,518M is bigger than pre-tax income of $6,869M.

takeaways.title: A cash machine
takeaways.text: Free cash flow was $7,466M — 41% of revenue — because capital spending was only $237M. Broadcom raised its quarterly dividend 10% to $0.65 a share on the strength of it.

oneTimers: The $1,649M tax benefit includes a one-time discrete non-cash tax benefit of about $2.1B from the lapse of statutes of limitations on old tax positions — it flatters this quarter's bottom line and will not repeat on schedule.

GAAP profit carries $2,052M of amortization of acquisition-related intangible assets ($1,545M inside cost of revenue and $507M inside operating expenses) — mostly bookkeeping from the VMware deal, not cash. On Broadcom's non-GAAP view, net income was $9,714M instead of $8,518M.
otherDetail: Interest expense of $761M on Broadcom's debt, partly offset by $122M of other income — a net -$639M below operating profit.
taxBenefitDetail: A $1,649M income-tax benefit — including a one-time ~$2.1B non-cash benefit from lapsed tax statutes of limitations — added to the bottom line instead of reducing it.
